_about: Aristophanes in English, translator per title. Complete: The Eleven Comedies, 'now for the first time literally and completely translated' (anonymous, The Athenian Society, 1912), 2 vols. Single plays: W. J. Hickie's prose Clouds (Bohn), B. B. Rogers's verse Frogs, Jack Lindsay's Lysistrata (1926; Gutenberg treats it as US public domain; Lindsay d. 1990, so not PD in life+70 countries). PG 3012, 2571 and 3013 were checked by 8-word shingle overlap (0.85-0.87) and are the Athenian Society translation split out, so they are excluded as duplicates. Added 2026-10-03, raw IA OCR: B. D. Walsh's Acharnians, Knights and Clouds (Bohn, 1848); the 1812 Valpy Comedies (Clouds, Plutus, Frogs, Birds; the volume names Cumberland and Dunster, the rest unnamed); an anonymous Oxford literal Plutus and Frogs (Talboys, 1822); and the Acharnians in verse by C. J. Billson (1882) and R. Y. Tyrrell (1883). Added 2026-10-03 (later), raw IA OCR from Google scans: Thomas Mitchell's Comedies vol. I (London, 1820), completing his set with vol. II above; and W. J. Hickie's Bohn vol. II (title page MDCCCLIII, 1853; IA's record says 1822, which is wrong), completing aristophanes-hickie-1887-v1 with the five later plays. B. B. Rogers's Bell editions, Greek facing: the Clouds (1852, his first version), Peace (1913) and Birds (1906), filling the Loeb vol. II gap; and his free Lysistrata, The Revolt of the Women (1878), raw IA.

_excluded.B. B. Rogers's complete Aristophanes (Be: Rogers's translation is held from the 1924 Loeb, vols. I and III (aristophanes-rogers-loeb-*). Vol. II (Peace, Birds, Frogs) is on Internet Archive only as lending copies, so Peace and Birds are now held from the Bell editions (1913, 1906) and the Frogs is held clean from Gutenberg. The other Bell editions (Wasps 1875, Plutus 1907, Ecclesiazusae 1917, Lysistrata and Thesmophoriazusae 1911, Frogs 1919) were scanned cleanly but not added: their translation duplicates the Loeb, and their extra matter is Greek text and commentary. Add them if the commentary is wanted.
_excluded.J. Hookham Frere (1840): three of the four plays held from the Morley volume (aristophanes-frere-morley, 1887); the fourth, the Frogs, is now held from Everyman vol. II (aristophanes-frere-frogs-everyman-1911)
